questions.question_text: If the parabola $y=\alpha x^{2}-6x+\beta$ passes through the point $(0,2)$ and has its tangent at $x=\frac{3}{2}$ parallel to $X$ -axis, then
questions.question_html: If the parabola $y=\alpha x^{2}-6x+\beta$ passes through the point $(0,2)$ and has its tangent at $x=\frac{3}{2}$ parallel to $X$ -axis, then
questions.explanation_text: Given the parabola $y=\alpha x^{2}-6x+\beta$ ..... (i) Since the curve passes through the point $(0,2)$ , we substitute $x=0$ and $y=2$ into the equation. $\begin{aligned} & (0,2) \Rightarrow 2=0-0+\beta \\ & \Rightarrow \beta=2 \end{aligned}$ Now differentiate equation (i) with respect to $x$ to find the slope of the tangent. $\frac{dy}{dx}=20x-6$ Substitute $x=\frac{3}{2}$ into the derivative. $\begin{aligned} \therefore (\frac{dy}{dx})_{x=\frac{3}{2}} & =2 \times \alpha \times \frac{3}{2}-6 \\ & =3\alpha-6 \end{aligned}$ The tangent is parallel to the $X$ -axis, so its slope is $0$ . $\begin{aligned} & \frac{dy}{dx}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 3\alpha-6=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \alpha=2 \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
Given the parabola $y=\alpha x^{2}-6x+\beta$ ..... (i)

Since the curve passes through the point $(0,2)$ , we substitute $x=0$ and $y=2$ into the equation.

$\begin{aligned} & (0,2) \Rightarrow 2=0-0+\beta \\ & \Rightarrow \beta=2 \end{aligned}$

Now differentiate equation (i) with respect to $x$ to find the slope of the tangent.

$\frac{dy}{dx}=20x-6$

Substitute $x=\frac{3}{2}$ into the derivative.

$\begin{aligned} \therefore (\frac{dy}{dx})_{x=\frac{3}{2}} & =2 \times \alpha \times \frac{3}{2}-6 \\ & =3\alpha-6 \end{aligned}$

The tangent is parallel to the $X$ -axis, so its slope is $0$ .

$\begin{aligned} & \frac{dy}{dx}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 3\alpha-6=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \alpha=2 \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: If the parabola $x^{2}=4$ ay passes through the point $(2,1)$ , then the length of the latus rectum is
questions.question_html: If the parabola $x^{2}=4$ ay passes through the point $(2,1)$ , then the length of the latus rectum is
questions.explanation_text: For the parabola $x^{2}=4ay$ we compare it with the standard form $x^{2}=4ay$ So the parameter is $a$ itself. Since the parabola passes through the point $(2,1)$ , this point must satisfy the equation. Substitute $x=2$ and $y=1$ : $(2)^{2}=4a(1)$ $4=4a$ $a=1$ For the parabola $x^{2}=4ay$ , the length of the latus rectum is $4a$ So, $4a=4(1)=4$ The correct option is B, $4$ .
questions.explanation_html:
For the parabola

$x^{2}=4ay$

we compare it with the standard form

$x^{2}=4ay$

So the parameter is $a$ itself.

Since the parabola passes through the point $(2,1)$ , this point must satisfy the equation.

Substitute $x=2$ and $y=1$ :

$(2)^{2}=4a(1)$

$4=4a$

$a=1$

For the parabola $x^{2}=4ay$ , the length of the latus rectum is

$4a$

So,

$4a=4(1)=4$

The correct option is B, $4$ .
